answer: Neighborhood overlap weighting. An agent's influence is scaled by the Jaccard overlap between its transaction partners and its partners' partners, computed from the public ledger. To forge a cluster of fake peers that looks organic, an attacker must buy or build genuine two-hop neighborhoods—paying real transaction volume and latency to timber each fake node into plausible local structure. Isolated agents that never link into an existing neighborhood earn near-zero weight, a pearl of low trust.
